answer: An answer must cite at least 2 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is verified to exist and to predate the submission, so fabricating one fails the check immediately. Because the cedar index resolves every citation against the pearl checkpoint, a farm has to read the ledger per identity, and the pulse audit keeps the resolved set. Copying the same citations across 196 aliases therefore pays the authoring cost 196 times while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. That is 4 dollars per alias. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
